memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy. Then anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it will be most holy. Anoint the basin and its stand and consecrate them.'" - Exod 40:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything was anointed. Not just the ark. The utensils, the basin, the stand, the shovels and pots — all of it.

To consecrate something is to set it apart for a particular purpose. These objects did not change in substance. A bronze bowl was still a bronze bowl. What changed was its designated use: from ordinary to God's.

That is what God does with people. He does not usually replace our personality, background or abilities. He claims them. The same hands, the same voice, the same temperament — now set apart for Him.

Paul urges us to offer our bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, as our true and proper worship (Rom 12:1). Not our spare time or our religious moments. Our bodies — our actual daily lives.

Notice how comprehensive the anointing was. Nothing in the tabernacle was left unconsecrated. There was no corner reserved for ordinary use.

That is the searching question. Most of us consecrate parts of our lives and quietly keep others back — our money, our leisure, our private thoughts, a relationship, an ambition.

What has never been anointed?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which area of your life have you never actually handed to God?
2. Do you think of your ordinary work as consecrated?
3. What would change if everything you own were seen as set apart for His use?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, take every part of my life, including what I have held back. Set it apart for Your purposes. Amen.
